content.text:
I've submitted index 62 (Fe 0.39, Ni 0.18, V 0.42) as the best composition, at a photocurrent of 7.5e-7 A. With only 3 measurements across 160 candidates, this is a best guess: I don't know how close it is to the library's true best.

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| **62** | 0.39 / 0.18 / 0.42 | **7.5e-7** |
| 159 | 0.58 / 0.22 / 0.20 (Fe-rich) | 5.3e-7 |
| 90 | 0.34 / 0.17 / 0.48 (more V) | 5.3e-7 |

- **Why these three:** I picked them from the general assumption that Fe–V oxides with roughly equal Fe and V (like FeVO4) make better photoanodes than Ni vanadates. I didn't use the library's own data to choose them.
- **What the results suggest:** Moving away from roughly equal Fe and V in either direction lowered the photocurrent, so the best region is probably Fe:V near 1:1 with little Ni. Three points can't confirm that.
- **Tools I didn't use:** The list of known crystal phases was too long to return and I couldn't open the file it was saved to. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present is unchecked.
